explain: Swapping the schedule alone is not enough. The outputs are computed at the start of the cycle, before any rule runs (interfaces runs first), and the consumer learns about an item only through them. With enq ≫ deq alone, the registers do the right thing, but deq_valid is still count != 0 = false: the consumer sees nothing, and the item is dequeued unseen. (Try it: cycle 2 then has deq_valid = 0 although both rules fire.) So the outputs must look at the incoming item too, and a full bypass FIFO cannot take an item just because one leaves: enq runs first and sees count = 2, so enq_ready is count != 2.

The empty-FIFO cycle, in order (cycle 2 of the simulation: enq_valid high, deq_ready high, count = 0). 1. interfaces runs: enq_ready is 1; deq_valid is count != 0 || enq_valid = 1; deq_data is enq_data (9), because the queue is empty. The consumer sees the item. 2. enq runs: count is 0, so it fires and stores 9, count becomes 1. 3. deq runs and sees count = 1: deq_ready is high, so it fires and count goes back to 0. At cycle 3 the FIFO is empty again: the item went in and out in one cycle.

+  method Bit#(8) deq_data  = count == 0 ? enq_data : data[rp];
+-- The proof above is for the original design; it does not apply to this variant.
-/-- The registers after one clock cycle of the design itself. -/
-def next (reset enq : BitVec 1) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
-  let t := mkPipeFifo2.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons enq (.cons x (.cons deq .nil))))
-/-- Write `x` into slot `i` of the packed 2 x 8-bit vector. -/
-  (if i = 1#1 then x else d.extractLsb' 8 8) ++ (if i = 0#1 then x else d.extractLsb' 0 8)
-  ⟨s.data, s.wp, if fires then s.rp + 1#1 else s.rp, if fires then s.count - 1#2 else s.count⟩
-  let fires := enq = 1#1 ∧ s.count ≠ 2#2      -- s.count is what deq left
-  ⟨if fires then put s.data s.wp x else s.data, if fires then s.wp + 1#1 else s.wp, s.rp,
-    if fires then s.count + 1#2 else s.count⟩
-  ⟨s.data, if reset = 1#1 then 0#1 else s.wp, if reset = 1#1 then 0#1 else s.rp,
-/-- The cycle is the schedule `deq ≫ enq ≫ clear`, one rule after another. -/
-theorem next_eq_steps (reset enq : BitVec 1) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) :
-    next reset enq x deq s = clearStep reset (enqStep enq x (deqStep deq s)) := by
-    Sched.run, Action.step, Action.fires, writesIf, State.write, State.cur, State.read, HList.set,
-    HList.get, Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, Common.putR, Common.putW, Common.memAt,
-/-- A full FIFO that dequeues also accepts: it is full again afterwards. -/
-/-- A full FIFO that is not dequeued refuses: nothing changes. -/

explain: Read it from empty (cycle 1; the reset cycle 0 left the FIFO empty). 1. deq has nothing to take. 2. enq runs and stores the item, count = 1. From cycle 2 on, count is 1 at the start of every cycle: 1. deq takes the oldest item, count = 0. 2. enq sees count = 0 and stores the new item, count = 1. So in steady state the FIFO holds one item, deq_valid first goes high at cycle 2, and one item leaves and one enters every cycle.
